home: Inkpaw — a Hyprland desktop drawn in ink
Inkpaw is a complete, modular Hyprland 0.56 desktop in Lua: themed from your wallpaper, configured from one Settings app, with a hand-drawn ink and parchment style.
install: Install Inkpaw on Arch Linux with one command. It adds a login session next to your usual one and never writes to ~/.config.
screenshots: Every screen of Inkpaw: desktop, Spotlight, quick panel, AI assistant, Settings, selectors, cheat sheet, power menu, lock screen.
docs: How Inkpaw works: installation, configuration, theming, the bar, the apps, keybindings and development.

home.title: A desktop drawn in ink.
home.lead: Inkpaw is a complete, modular Hyprland setup: bar, launcher, menus, quick panel, lock screen and an AI assistant — themed from your wallpaper and configured from one Settings app.
home.logo_alt: Inkpaw logo: an ochre cat asleep above the name

home.features_lead: Each part is a module you can switch off, every file is commented, and every value lives in hypr/settings.conf.
features: Pick a wallpaper and everything follows: borders, bar, menus, notifications, terminal, GTK apps and Firefox. Nine static themes, light and dark.
A GTK 4 window for every option — bar layout, fonts, gaps, monitors, keyboard, default apps, AI provider. Live, with a reset on every row.
Apps, calculator, files, emoji, clipboard, web and maps, desktop actions — one list with a titled section for each.
Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, sound per app, brightness with DDC/CI, battery and power mode, notifications, calendar, media — instant drop-downs.
A side window that docks beside your tiled windows. Conversations, full Markdown, Claude or any OpenAI-compatible API.
One concern per file, a module per line. ./test.sh verify checks every monitor profile and renders every theme in a throw-away copy.
home.how_p1: Inkpaw installs as a second session in your login screen. At every login it builds its own config root — links to the repo for its apps, links to your real ~/.config for everything else — and starts Hyprland on it.
home.how_p2: Your browser, editor and chat apps keep their settings. Your usual session is untouched. Remove one desktop file and Inkpaw is gone.
how_steps: It clones the repo, installs the missing packages and draws the wallpapers — asking first.
Log out and choose the new session in your login screen. A welcome window opens.
<kbd>SUPER</kbd>+<kbd>CTRL</kbd>+<kbd>S</kbd> for Settings, <kbd>SUPER</kbd>+<kbd>CTRL</kbd>+<kbd>K</kbd> for every shortcut. Your edits to the repo are live.
home.duo_title: Day or night, glass or ink
home.duo_text: Flip light and dark with <kbd>SUPER</kbd> + <kbd>CTRL</kbd> + <kbd>T</kbd>. Prefer a quieter look? Switch the interface style back to the soft-glass default in Settings — your colors, wallpaper and windows stay as they are.

install.title: Install in one line
install.lead: On Arch Linux or an Arch-based distribution with Hyprland 0.56 or newer. Inkpaw adds a session next to your usual one and never writes to ~/.config.
install.cmd_note: Want to read it first? git clone the repo and run ./install.sh from it — same steps.
install.steps_title: What it does — asking each time
steps: Clones Inkpaw into ~/.local/share/inkpaw/repo, or updates it.
Hyprland, Waybar, swaync, matugen, Walker… with yay or paru.
Keeps your system layout (localectl) as your setting.
15 procedural wallpapers into ~/Pictures/wallpapers, about a minute.
“Hyprland — Inkpaw” in your login screen, with sudo.
install.opt_note: Passed after bash -s -- when piped, e.g. … | bash -s -- --yes --sddm-theme
options: also install the hand-drawn SDDM login screen
do not add the login session — no sudo at all
needs: Arch Linux, or a distribution based on it
a login screen that reads Wayland sessions — SDDM, GDM, ly…
yay or paru for the AUR packages (Walker, Elephant)
install.needs_note: ./test.sh deps lists what is missing and prints the exact install command.
install.un_text: Remove the session and Inkpaw's own folders. Your ~/.config was never modified.

guides.title: Installation
guides.lead: One line on Arch Linux, a login session next to your usual one, nothing written to ~/.config.
blocks: The installer asks before every step that installs something or needs sudo: files, packages, keyboard layout, wallpapers, login session. See the install page for its options.

At every login session/start.sh rebuilds ~/.local/share/inkpaw/session-root: links to the repo for Inkpaw’s folders, links to your real ~/.config for everything else. It then sets XDG_CONFIG_HOME to it and starts Hyprland.
Inkpaw’s own state lives in ~/.local/state/inkpaw (your settings, last theme, conversations, notification history) and ~/.cache/inkpaw.
pick your usual session, read ~/.local/share/inkpaw/session.log, run ./test.sh verify
Updating is a git pull in the repo (or running the installer again). Your settings live outside the repo and survive updates.

guides.title: Configuration
guides.lead: Every value lives in one file, every change in Settings is a line of state — your defaults are never rewritten.
blocks: every user value: apps, keyboard, monitors, gaps, borders, fonts, bar, wallpaper folder…
what you changed in Settings — overrides settings.conf
the last theme, restored at login
The Settings window and the rofi menu are both generated from hypr/settings.schema, one line per option:

Page/Group | KEY | type | choices | label | apply
Bar/Layout | BAR_POSITION | choice | top,bottom | Position | bar
apply says what to reload: hypr, bar, theme, mode, scheme, skin, apps… Everything is also scriptable:

hypr/scripts/menus/settings.sh set BAR_POSITION bottom
hypr/scripts/menus/settings.sh unset BAR_POSITION
hypr/hyprland.lua only contains require() lines, one per concern in hypr/conf/. Comment one to switch a module off; press SUPER+CTRL+R to reload.
To expose any other settings.conf key in Settings, add one line to the schema.

guides.title: Theming
guides.lead: Pick a wallpaper, and matugen turns it into a palette for every app — or pick one of nine static themes.
blocks:
hyprtheme/theme.sh wallpaper ~/Pictures/x.jpg
hyprtheme/theme.sh static nord
hyprtheme/theme.sh mode dark
hyprtheme/generate-wallpapers.sh draws 15 procedural wallpapers with ImageMagick. Your own images go in the same folder.

One file in hyprtheme/templates/ whose first lines say where it goes: @output: <path>. Use {{colors.primary.default.hex}}, {{accent.a1}}, {{ansi.red}}, {{ui.font}}… and add a hook to live-reload the app.
Settings → Appearance → Interface style. Fonts, apps and the top bar turn hand-drawn — parchment panels, ink outlines, brush titles and cats — while colors, wallpaper and windows stay yours.

guides.title: The bar
guides.lead: Waybar is generated from a few settings: you never edit its JSON by hand.
blocks: capsules, floating, solid, minimal, hyde, encre
the ordered modules of each capsule

Waybar switches workspace with the legacy dispatch workspace N, which a Lua config rejects: waybar/ipc-proxy.py rewrites it into Lua. Every click command is detached with setsid, so an app opened from the bar survives a theme change.

guides.title: Apps
guides.lead: Spotlight, the quick panel, notifications, the AI assistant and the menus.
blocks: SUPER+SPACE. One list with a section per kind: calculator, apps, actions, files, emoji, clipboard, web and maps, command. Prefixes search one section: = calc, / files, . emoji, : clipboard, @ web, > run.

Click an icon of the bar: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, sound per app, brightness (DDC/CI for external screens, night light), battery and power mode, notifications history, calendar, media. It stays in memory, so it opens at once.

<kbd>SUPER</kbd>+<kbd>I</kbd>. A window that docks beside your tiled windows, with conversations (<kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>O</kbd>, <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>N</kbd>), streaming Markdown and Copy buttons. Claude by default; OpenAI, Ollama, OpenRouter or any compatible endpoint in Settings.
API keys are stored in ~/.local/state/inkpaw/secrets.conf (mode 600), never in the repo.

guides.title: Keybindings
guides.lead: MOD is SUPER. The live, searchable list is SUPER+CTRL+K — generated from every bind’s description.
blocks: go to workspace 1–10 (AZERTY: the number row)
screenshot an area and annotate it

guides.title: Development
guides.lead: One concern per file, every value in settings.conf, generated files never committed.
blocks:
./test.sh deps            # missing packages + the install command
./test.sh verify          # every monitor profile, every file, every theme
./test.sh nested          # the whole desktop in a nested window
a line in settings.conf + one in settings.schema
a line with a description in hypr/conf/keybinds/
./test.sh verify must pass before every commit — it runs in a throw-away copy, never in your config.
